_note: Reported news for the PDF. Compiled every Sunday from the climate-news monitor sources (Eye Radio, Radio Tamazuj, Sudans Post, UN/UNMISS, ReliefWeb, Radio Yei, others); last compiled 2026-10-11 and verified 10 times against the article links. 'counties' lists every county the item names; items with no county go in scope 'national' (state or countrywide). Items older than NEWS_DAYS (21) are dropped. 'compiled' and 'verified_passes' are written only after all verification passes finish; the county bulletin workflow (news_gate.py) holds the weekly email and the social posts until they show this week's compile.

items.text: No Ebola case has been confirmed in South Sudan; the health system is on high alert after Kenya confirmed its first case (the patient died on 5 October) and with a large outbreak in DR Congo.

Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation warns of possible Nile flooding, including in and around Juba: simulations suggest Lake Victoria could rise above its historical maximum, and ICPAC sees a higher El Nino likelihood with above-normal rain over the lake basin. Readings from Nimule to Renk and Nasir to Bentiu are falling and below alert levels. Reduced June-September rainfall has also affected several states and the administrative areas of Abyei, Pibor and Ruweng.

Heavy rains and insecurity have left Ibba communities more isolated: the roughly 100 km Yambio-Ibba road is almost impassable (deep potholes, mud and flooding), regularly slowing vehicles to almost walking pace.

Flooding has submerged about 70% of the land around Bentiu; about 300,000 people shelter behind dykes built and maintained by UNMISS and IOM, and UNMISS's Bentiu head estimates 50,000 could be submerged if a breach is not repaired within ten hours and dyke work is disrupted. IOM faces a shortage of resources for dyke maintenance and pumping; heavy rain is expected with El Nino from October to February (county inferred from Bentiu).

Lakes State's Akut-dor peace committee (datelined Rumbek) was restructured to bring in younger cattle-camp leaders, as heavy rains and flooding raise concerns about renewed communal violence; a community leader says flooding could force cattle camps to move to higher ground (county not stated).

UNMISS-backed peace dialogue in Maban discussed flooding and drought as climate shocks; a paramount chief said the prolonged lack of rain is hurting communities more than ever this year. Early warning and evacuation planning were discussed (no figures given).

State health officials report 40 hepatitis E cases, no deaths so far, over two weeks in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (counties including Aweil East, Aweil North, Gok Machar and Aweil West), which they link to water contaminated during the rains.

Flash floods after heavy rain disrupted movement between Kapuri and Juba; according to residents, rising water submerged the Kapuri bridge and left travellers stranded on both sides (county inferred from location).

Heavy rain flooded several IDP camps and damaged makeshift shelters; the relief commission coordinator says families in 15 camps across three payams struggle to get food and basic aid, an IDP representative says there are no medicines, and food prices have risen.
Seven-day cholera vaccination drive with MSF and WHO targets more than 100,000 displaced people (an official says it could reach more) after thousands of cholera cases in Unity State this year.

State officials, citing a rapid assessment, say about 1.1 million people are affected by a prolonged rainfall deficit across five counties (not named); they fear more hunger later this year and into 2027.

Water Resources Minister says Uganda's notice anticipates high Lake Victoria levels, which he expects to reach record highs, with increased releases into the Nile that could cause severe riverine flooding, particularly around Juba and other low-lying areas. Nile readings from Nimule to Renk and Nasir to Bentiu are below alert levels but, he says, will change rapidly as high flows arrive.
